Check that the limbs of a rating meet

Source: R/check_limb_continuity.R
check_limb_continuity.Rd

At each junction between two limbs, measures how far apart the two equations are at the stage they share, three ways:

  • the discharge gap, in m\(^3\)/s (gap_cms) and as a fraction of the discharge below the junction (gap_rel);

  • the stage gap (stage_gap_m): how far the upper limb would have to move sideways to meet the lower one, which is the number a gauge reader sees as the rating jumping at that stage. It is negative when the upper limb is the higher curve;

  • the change of slope (slope_change_pct): the difference in \(dQ/dH\) across the junction. A change of slope at a breakpoint is normal, because that is what a breakpoint is for, so it is reported but judged only if you give tol_slope.

A junction is continuous when the discharge gap and the stage gap are both within tolerance. The discharge gap passes if it is within tol_abs or within tol_rel, so a tiny flow is not failed on a percentage and a large flow does not need a fraction of a cumec; the stage gap passes if it is within tol_stage.

It works from the equations, exactly at the shared stage, where detect_rc_gaps() scans a discretised rating table. With after it reports the same measures before and after an alignment (align_limb_equations() or align_limb_boundaries()), so the effect of the amendment is on the table and not only claimed.

A single limb has no junction, and a FlodeSegmentedRating is continuous by construction (every later factor of its joint equation is exactly 1 at its breakpoint), so each gives a table with no rows.

Usage

check_limb_continuity(
  x,
  after = NULL,
  tol_abs = 0.05,
  tol_rel = 0.01,
  tol_stage = 0.005,
  tol_slope = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A FlodeRating or FlodeRatingTable.

after

NULL (default), or the same rating after an alignment, with the same number of limbs, to compare with x.

tol_abs

Number, m\(^3\)/s. Default 0.05.

tol_rel

Number. Default 0.01 (1%).

tol_stage

Number, metres. Default 0.005, about the resolution of a gauge.

tol_slope

Number or NULL. A change of slope larger than this fraction (0.1 is 10%) is reported as slope_ok = FALSE. NULL (default): the slope is reported, not judged, and slope_ok is NA.

Value

A data.table, one row per junction, with junction, stage_m, limb_below, limb_above, q_below_cms, q_above_cms, gap_cms, gap_rel, stage_gap_m, slope_below, slope_above, slope_change_pct, discharge_ok, stage_ok, slope_ok and continuous.

With after, one row per junction with junction and, for stage_m, gap_cms, gap_rel, stage_gap_m, slope_change_pct and continuous, a _before and an _after column, and improved, TRUE where the discharge gap shrank. Boundaries can move in align_limb_boundaries(), so the junction stage is given for both.

See also

detect_rc_gaps(), align_limb_equations(), align_limb_boundaries(), rating_invariants() for the same question as a warning

Examples

# Two limbs that do not quite meet at 1 m.
rating <- FlodeRatingTable(table = data.table::data.table(
  lower_level = c(0.2, 1), upper_level = c(1, 3),
  C = c(2, 2.1), a = c(0, 0), n = c(1.5, 1.6)
))
check_limb_continuity(rating)[, .(stage_m, gap_cms, gap_rel, stage_gap_m, continuous)]
#>    stage_m gap_cms gap_rel stage_gap_m continuous
#>      <num>   <num>   <num>       <num>     <lgcl>
#> 1:       1     0.1    0.05 -0.03003361      FALSE

# Before and after closing the gap.
aligned <- align_limb_equations(rating)
check_limb_continuity(rating, after = aligned)[, .(gap_cms_before, gap_cms_after, improved)]
#>    gap_cms_before gap_cms_after improved
#>             <num>         <num>   <lgcl>
#> 1:            0.1             0     TRUE
